why.title: Why this flow
why.rcOnBranch: Nothing publishes a release candidate (no workflow starts on its tag): a candidate is tagged on {rc} and reaches neither {release} nor the trunk.
why.mergeBack: The release comes back to {trunk} by a pull request merged with a merge commit, never squash or rebase, so that {release} stays in {trunk}'s history and the branches do not diverge again.
why.ticket: The project's commits name a ticket (chore(#N): …): the release's commits name the ticket of the version's milestone titled “Release vX.Y.Z”, or the one given with --ticket.

agentChoice.subtitle: {branch} → {base}

what.rebase: {agent} rebases {branch} on {base} in an isolated copy of the branch, resolves the conflicts, runs the project's checks and pushes with lease.
what.restart: {agent} applies review round {round}'s comments on {branch} in an isolated copy of the branch, commits, pushes and replies on each thread.
what.investigate: {agent} resolves what blocks {branch} in an isolated copy of the branch, in this order: {checks}. It finds the cause of each (a fix pushed on the branch, a rebase pushed with lease, the local CI run until green, a rerun of a flaky job with its ticket). It never merges and asks you only for a real decision.
what.finish: {agent} checks {branch} against its ticket in an isolated copy of the branch and finishes what is left: conflicts with {base}, red CI, requested changes. It pushes with lease and never merges.

background.text: Nothing opens and nothing takes the focus. Follow it in the pull request's row in the Control room or in Sessions; a notification tells you when it is done or needs you.
